title: Smoothie Blender Animation Sequencer
description: The user operates a virtual smoothie blender station where an avocado and water bottle sit on a conveyor belt. The user must choreograph a multi-step animation sequence: drag ingredients onto the blender platform, set rotation speeds, configure pour timing for the water bottle, and blend the avocado with precise keyframe controls. An energy conservation system tracks total kinetic energy across all animated objects, and full undo/redo support lets the user refine the sequence.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Smoothie Blender Animation Sequencer. Load Avocado.glb and WaterBottle.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: place a simple blender platform (cylinder geometry, semi-transparent glass material) at center, a conveyor belt (animated plane with scrolling texture) on the left, and a results pedestal on the right. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0,3,5) with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4 intensity), a directional light from above-right, and a point light inside the blender cylinder for glow effect. Interactions (10-14 steps): 1) Click avocado to select it. 2) Drag avocado onto conveyor belt start position. 3) Click play to animate avocado sliding along conveyor to blender. 4) Click water bottle to select it. 5) Drag water bottle above blender and set tilt angle using a slider (0-90 degrees) to control pour animation. 6) Press pour button to animate water bottle tilting and a particle stream flowing into blender. 7) Use a speed slider to set blender spin RPM (affects avocado spin animation inside). 8) Press blend button to trigger combined spin animation of both objects. 9) Use a timeline scrubber to adjust keyframe timing of the full sequence. 10) Press undo to revert last action. 11) Press redo to reapply. 12) Adjust energy coupling: a displayed kinetic energy bar must remain conserved — increasing water pour speed decreases avocado spin speed proportionally. 13) Press export to play the full choreographed animation start to finish. Implement an action history stack for undo/redo supporting all parameter changes and drag operations. Display a HUD showing current kinetic energy total, step count, and active object name. All animations should use requestAnimationFrame with smooth easing. The energy conservation law means totalKE = 0.5*m1*v1^2 + 0.5*m2*v2^2 must remain constant when user adjusts either speed slider, automatically coupling the other value.
